findings: OVERALL VERDICT — REFUTED: blog/46-what-time-is-electricity-cheapest.md attributes ~$0.2233/kWh off-peak and ~$0.4497/kWh peak to Con Edison's residential TOU (lines 37, 46, source[2] = coned.com/en/accounts-billing/your-bill/time-of-use). Re-fetched that source 2026-08-29; it shows NO 22.33c/44.97c values anywhere. The attribution itself is wrong for the cited page.

Correct current Con Ed residential TOU figures (live page, retrieved 2026-08-29): Jun 1–Sep 30 peak (8am–midnight) $0.2786/kWh; all other months peak $0.1711/kWh; off-peak (all other hours, all year) $0.0522/kWh; delivery 8am–midnight $0.16402/kWh (>250 kWh tier $0.18858 summer); monthly customer charge $21.00. Supply/delivery are itemized and the page notes rates exclude surcharges.

Article's supporting hour/period claims DO match the source: off-peak = midnight–8am weekdays + all weekend; peak = 8am–midnight; super-peak = Jun–Sep weekdays 2–6pm. These are CONFIRMED; only the price figures are refuted.

The 50% off-peak discount claim (line 56, 46) is also false on live Con Ed numbers: off-peak 5.22c vs summer peak 27.86c = an ~81% discount; vs winter peak 17.11c = ~70%. ~50% only holds on the erroneous 22.33/44.97 pair.
